questions.q: In the poem "वक्ष, फेयद्ज़ चप्किं", who is the primary addressee of the speaker's appeal, and what grammatical form indicates this address?
questions.a: The primary addressee is an implied listener/companion addressed as "वक्ष" (come) and "चप्किं" (let's cover - first person plural imperative), indicating a collective call to action. A wrong answer (e.g., identifying the poet as speaking to himself, or to God) reveals the student misses the communal/collective dimension of the appeal and the grammatical marker of shared responsibility in "चप्किं" (let us cover).

questions.q: Explain in your own words why the poet includes both natural elements (like मिट्टी, रात, धूप) and human activities (like ह्क्र्ज, क्स्र्क्स, फेह) in the same list of things to be protected.
questions.a: The poet blends nature and human life because in an agrarian society they are inseparable: the soil feeds the crops the farmer ploughs, the night cools the bulls that pull the plough, the sun ripens the grain that becomes food. A wrong answer treating them as separate categories shows the student hasn't grasped the poem's ecological worldview where human survival is woven into natural cycles—a core concept for Class 11 rural sociology links.

questions.q: Apply the concept of "personification as supporting character" to the line "ह्क्र्ज की व्क्स, ऋकु्क की म्क्ज्ह". What human vulnerability is projected onto the deer and the season, and why does this matter for the poem's argument?
questions.a: The deer's fear (व्क्स) and the season's fragility (म्क्ज्ह) are projected human anxieties: the deer represents innocent life threatened by habitat loss, the season represents the predictable natural cycles farmers depend on. This matters because it expands "protection" from human concerns to the entire biosphere. A wrong answer that treats these as mere decorative images misses how personification makes ecological crisis emotionally immediate—a key analytical skill for board exams.

questions.q: Analyze how the progression from concrete nouns (मिट्टी, रात, धूप) to abstract nouns (ओक्य्ग्क्म्ह, व्द्क्मिउ, त्क>क:िउ) in the list of things to be covered changes the poem's emotional and intellectual demand on the reader.
questions.a: The shift moves the appeal from protecting tangible, visible things (soil, night) to protecting intangible human experiences (helplessness, the act of covering, the urge to understand). This deepens the poem from a conservation plea to a philosophical defense of rural consciousness itself. A wrong answer that only lists the nouns without analyzing the abstract-concrete trajectory shows inability to track structural progression—a skill tested in 6-mark board questions.

questions.q: Evaluate the effectiveness of the final stanza's shift to first-person plural ("हमारे", "हम") after the extended list of third-person entities. Does this strengthen or weaken the poem's call to collective action? Justify.
questions.a: It strengthens the call by making the speaker and addressee part of the very fabric they've been asked to protect—they ARE the "क्प्प्स-ल्ह मेह्न" (laughing-crying together) and "क्प्प्स-ल्स लिउस" (taking laughter-crying). The shift from "cover IT" to "cover US" closes the distance between protector and protected. A wrong answer calling it a mere pronoun change misses the rhetorical climax where the community recognizes its own vulnerability—a sophisticated evaluation expected in competency-based questions.

questions.q: Create a four-line stanza in the same style that adds a modern rural vulnerability (e.g., migrating youth, drying wells, chemical farming) to the poem's list, maintaining the rhythm and the imperative "वक्ष, फेयद्ज़ चप्किं" frame.
questions.a: A strong answer will mirror the poem's noun+postposition+verb pattern (e.g., "सूखे कुएँ की प्यास / बंजर खेत की साँस / उजड़े गाँव की आस / वक्ष, फेयद्ज़ चप्किं") and connect the new vulnerability to an existing poem element. A poor answer that just writes a generic slogan reveals inability to internalize the poem's structural logic and linguistic texture—the highest creative competency.
